newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq stocks close with 2.6 percent gain.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq stocks close with 2.6 percent gain.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks posted their second consecutive session of sharp gains on Monday, shooting higher as investors piled into second-tier stocks.
Traders said resurgent interest in small-capitalization stocks, in addition to fresh buying in larger-cap high technology issues, powered the Nasdaq rally.
The Nasdaq composite finished unofficially up 34 points, or 2.6 percent, to 1339. On Friday the index rose 2.7 percent in a 35-point rise that was its largest single-day gain.
The index was still shy of its January 22 record closing high of 1388.

"The big question is, is this a blowoff or the beginning of a bull market" in secondary stocks, said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president at Unterberg Harris. "I think it's the beginning of a bull market."
The Russell 2000 small-cap barometer rose more than eight points, or 2.4 percent, to 362.

Among special situations, Applied Materials Inc and Novellus Systems Inc said they reached a settlement in a patent dispute that calls for Novellus to pay $80 million in damages to Applied Materials. Applied Materials shot up 4-1/8 to 61-3/4 and Novellus rose 9-3/8 to 78-3/4.
